name: Mozilla TLS — Modern
reference: Mozilla Server Side TLS guideline, machine-readable version 5.7 (ssl-config.mozilla.org/guidelines/5.7.json), configurations.modern.
summary: The strongest interoperable profile: TLS 1.3 only, the three TLS 1.3 AEAD suites, ECDSA P-256/P-384 certificates.
notes: Corrected to Mozilla 5.7, which redefined Modern as TLS 1.3 ONLY: configurations.modern.tls_versions is ["TLSv1.3"] and configurations.modern.ciphersuites is exactly ["TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256", "TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384", "TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256"] (ciphers.openssl/iana are empty). This replaces the previous file, which allowed TLS 1.2 and RSA -- the pre-5.0 meaning of Modern -- and could not be traced to 5.7. certificate.min_ec_bits 256 comes from configurations.modern.certificate_curves ["prime256v1", "secp384r1"] and ecdh_param_size 256; disallow_sha1 from certificate_signatures being only ecdsa-with-SHA256/384/512. FLAG: Modern 5.7 is ECDSA-only (certificate_types ["ecdsa"], rsa_key_size null); this schema cannot express 'RSA certificate forbidden', so no min_rsa_bits is asserted -- an RSA leaf is judged only by the TLS 1.3 protocol/suite rules. HSTS (hsts_min_age 63072000) and OCSP stapling (ocsp_staple true) are set by 5.7 but are server-config recommendations reported elsewhere, not enforced by this transport-crypto profile.
